content: Duhkha daurmanasya angamejayatva shvasaprashvasa vikshepa sahabhuvah. (Grief, distress, physical tremors, and erratic breathing accompany a scattered mind).
author: Patanjali
explanation:
In the profound psychology of the Yoga Sutras, Patanjali outlines the systematic roadmap for stilling mental fluctuations into radiant, sovereign stillness.

This teaching (Duhkha daurmanasya angamejayatva shvasaprashvasa vikshepa sa...) focuses directly on duhkha and daurmanasya. When we clear away reactive illusions and anchor ourselves in timeless principles, the mind recovers its pristine clarity and inner resilience.

True realization is never an abstract intellectual debate—it is an active discipline lived through quiet integrity and conscious presence in everyday moments.
practicalInsight: Apply this teaching on duhkha today: take a deliberate pause before reacting, align your actions with quiet integrity, and refuse to let transient friction disturb your center.
reflectionPrompt: How can you embody deeper duhkha and daurmanasya in the primary challenge you are navigating right now?
